topic: Plant Growth Regulators: Auxins and Gibberellins
title: Why Do Plants Bend to Light? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
A window plant bends toward the light, a trimmed hedge grows bushier, and some rice seedlings grow so tall they fall over. Aarav asks: what makes a plant bend, and which part senses the light?

We meet the five kinds of plant growth regulators, zoom from a grass seedling to its coleoptile to the tip, and rerun the coleoptile experiments of Charles and Francis Darwin and F. W. Went. Then what auxins do, with apical dominance shown live, and the gibberellins from the bakane disease to sugarcane and bolting, with a pause and think, a worked example picking the right regulator, the exam trap about 2,4-D, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 93 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Why a window plant bends to light

0:58 Zoom ladder: seedling, coleoptile, tip
1:22 How auxin was found
1:59 What auxins do: apical dominance and more
2:45 Gibberellins and the bakane disease + pause and think
4:00 Worked example: pick the regulator
4:22 Exam trap: does 2,4-D kill every plant?
4:40 Practice question (NEET pattern)
5:05 Recap and three questions to answer
